title: Auto Loans: Combining Discounts into an Enrolled APR
content:
This rule fixes how the discounts that qualify at an Auto Loans autopay enrollment are combined and applied to produce the APR and discount list recorded with the enrollment.

## Rule

The relationship discount, as confirmed from checking records, and the autopay discount, as it stands at enrollment, are summed into one total discount. That total is held to the product's combined discount limit. The capped total is then subtracted a single time from the starting rate, meaning the rate with every recorded discount taken back out. If the figure reached is below the product's APR floor, the APR is the floor instead. The APR is written to two decimal places.

Which discounts made it into the rate determines the list stored with it: both autopay and relationship, autopay only, relationship only, or none.

## Condition, judgement, outcome

| Relationship discount confirmed | Autopay discount included | Total discount taken off | Discount list recorded |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the lesser of the two summed and the combined limit | both autopay and relationship |
| yes | no | the relationship discount, within the limit | relationship only |
| no | yes | the autopay discount, within the limit | autopay only |
| no | no | nothing | none |

In every row the floor applies to the figure obtained.

## Sample calculations (figures made up for the example)

- Starting rate 7.30; relationship and autopay discounts of 0.30 each; limit 0.50; floor 4.00. The total of 0.60 is held to 0.50 and the APR is 6.80.
- Same loan without the autopay discount: the total is 0.30 and the APR is 7.00.
- Starting rate 4.40 with a capped total of 0.50 and a floor of 4.00: 3.90 is below the floor, so the APR is 4.00.
